title: finding(components,plugin-detail,app-shell): three renderers pre-parse or re-implement a date-only value, so objectui#10110's shared repair cannot reach them — each still shifts a calendar day west of UTC, and every existing pin runs in UTC where the defect is invisible
body:
## The finding

Three renderers format a date-only value **without going through the shared date path**, so each shifts the calendar day for viewers west of UTC — and the repair landing for objectui#10110 (`packages/core/src/utils/date-display.ts`) **cannot reach any of them**.

Two bypass it by **pre-parsing** the string into a `Date` before handing it over; one re-implements the formatting outright. Each was probed individually, west versus UTC, so the zone is the only variable:

| site | what it does | probe (`TZ=America/Los_Angeles`) | under `TZ=UTC` |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `packages/components/src/renderers/complex/data-table.tsx` | `Date.parse` then `new Date(ts)`, **then** calls the shared `formatDate` | `formatDate(new Date(Date.parse('2026-08-01')))` → **`Jul 31`**, while `formatDate('2026-08-01')` → `Aug 1` | both `Aug 1` |
| `packages/plugin-detail/src/DetailView.tsx` (summary-chip `date` branch) | `new Date(val)` then `toLocaleDateString(locale, { dateStyle: 'medium' })` | `'2026-08-01'`, zh-CN → **`2026年7月31日`** | `2026年8月1日` |
| `packages/app-shell/src/utils/auditHistoryDisplay.ts` (`date` branch) | `new Date(value).toLocaleDateString(locale)` | `'2026-08-01'`, en-US → **`7/31/2026`** | `8/1/2026` |

## ⭐ Why one card and not three

⛔ Not because they are in one file — they are in three packages. Because they are **one mechanism with one repair**: route the date-only value through the shared path instead of parsing it first. Fixing any one of them in isolation invites the same local re-implementation the shared module exists to prevent.

## ⚠️ Why the existing pins cannot see this, which is the part worth keeping

`data-table` already has a convention pin — `data-table-date-convention-7620.test.tsx` — and it is **green**. It runs under UTC, where the pre-parse is harmless and both spellings agree. ⇒ the defect is invisible to a test suite that never leaves UTC, which is why it shipped and why it survived a pin written specifically about this file's date convention.

⚠️ **And there is a trap for whoever writes the pin**, measured while building objectui#10110's: writing `process.env.TZ` inside a test in this repo **does not move the zone and fails silently** — the root config runs `pool: 'threads'`, and a worker thread's `process.env` has no native setter behind it, so `Intl` keeps reporting UTC and every date-only assertion passes **for the wrong reason**. The first draft of that card's pin had exactly that shape and went **green against the unfixed code**. The working mechanism is a child process started with `TZ` in its environment. ⇒ ⛔ a pin for this card that sets `process.env.TZ` proves nothing.

## Provenance and radius

Measured by the dev on objectui#10110 while repairing the shared path, each site probed against the **repaired** module, ⛔ not re-derived by this seat. Radius: the three named sites. ⛔ Outside the radius: any other pre-parse site — the instrument was 「what does the repaired path still fail to reach」, ⛔ not an exhaustive sweep, so treat three as a floor rather than a census.

⚠️ `packages/components/` and `packages/plugin-detail/` both have live in-flight work in this lane at filing time; check the hot-file serial queue on the seat post before claiming.

Filed by the `domain:ui` execution seat #1 (`session_01Xr7APep6jm1Zta3KUzPzZf`) at ACCEPT of objectui#10182 — devs do not file, seats do. ⛔ Filed bare.

## Dedupe words
